invariant: An autarkic composite remains an independently solved state image when it contains entry or exit border points. Those points participate in the inner Graphviz topology as 12-by-12 port nodes, entry-point links do not create ordinary rank-same constraints, and the visible composite frontier is derived from normal interior boxes plus the border-point centers.
causal_divergence: Rust's autonomous-composite builders explicitly reject every EntryPoint and ExitPoint state. The diagram then falls through to the flat renderer, which emits the composite as an ordinary entity and solves its children in the root graph. Java instead keeps the group autarkic, selects EntityImageStateBorder for the non-normal leaves, solves the group's pure inner links through GroupMakerState, and applies Cluster.manageEntryExitPoint plus FrontierCalculator before wrapping that inner image. The missing group-local border-node and frontier model causes the repeated cluster-versus-entity structural divergence across the entry/exit fixture matrix.
planned_change: Extend the autonomous state model so entry and exit leaves remain inside their owning composite, carry PlantUML's border-port Graphviz semantics, and influence the solved composite frontier through a Rust port of the FrontierCalculator rules. Preserve Java's entry-point link constraint behavior in graph construction, then render the resulting group-local entities and links through the existing autonomous-composite emission path.
perturbation_axes: declaration order plus composite and interior label dimensions
